The solution allows on-site operators to connect with remote specialists in real time, reducing costly equipment downtime across manufacturing, automotive, aviation, and logistics industries. The application is now available and is being deployed with Fortune 500 companies.

headline: 1 Unstoppable Stock to Buy Now Before It Joins Nvidia, Apple, Alphabet, and Microsoft in the $3 Trillion Club
summary: Meta Platforms is positioned to join the $3 trillion market cap club, potentially offering 81% upside from current levels. The company leverages AI expertise to boost engagement and ad revenue across its 3.6 billion daily users. With expected 17% annual revenue growth and record capital expenditures of $125 billion planned for 2026, Meta could reach $3 trillion valuation by 2030 or sooner.

headline: 3 Artificial Intelligence (AI) Stocks That Could Make You a Millionaire
summary: The article highlights three AI infrastructure stocks as alternatives to Nvidia for building wealth: Broadcom, which creates custom AI chips (ASICs) for major clients like Anthropic and OpenAI; Lam Research, which supplies wafer-processing equipment to chip foundries; and TSMC, the world's largest semiconductor foundry specializing in advanced chip manufacturing. These companies benefit from the massive AI buildout and offer diversification within the AI sector.

headline: Post-Subsidy Landscape: From Subsidy Reliance To Tech Appreciation In China's 3C market
summary: China's 2026 consumer subsidy program has narrowed coverage but spurred stronger demand for mid- to high-end 3C electronics and home appliances with AI capabilities. Despite rising raw material costs forcing price increases, consumers are shifting from basic renewals to quality upgrades, with AI-equipped appliances accounting for nearly 60% of sales. Manufacturers are prioritizing high-margin, feature-rich products as subsidy stimulus effects diminish.

headline: Does Apple Have a New Hit Product? I Think So!
summary: Apple's new $599 Mac Neo is positioned as a major hit product that opens up a new budget market segment. Rather than focusing on direct Mac sales profits, the strategy aims to expand Apple's ecosystem and drive long-term services revenue growth, which is the company's second-largest business segment.

headline: Pixalate Launches DEFASED Pre-Bid Blocklist: A Daily Updated List of Apps Delisted From Google Play and Apple App Store — With Bundle ID, App Name, Removal Date for 100+ Countries
summary: Pixalate announced the general availability of its DEFASED pre-bid blocklists, identifying over 7.8 million mobile apps removed from Google Play Store and Apple App Store across 100+ countries. The daily updated feeds help SSPs, exchanges, and DSPs block delisted apps that may still generate ad impressions and pose fraud or privacy risks. Data is available via FTP, AWS RTB Fabric, Enrichment API, and Pixalate's analytics dashboard.

headline: How Netflix Stock Gained 15.3% Last Month
summary: Netflix stock rose 15.3% in February 2026 after the company canceled its $83 billion bid for Warner Bros. Discovery, avoiding a massive debt burden that would have multiplied its debt load 5-6 times. While the company faces competitive pressures from Disney, Amazon, and Apple, it has growth opportunities in ad-supported streaming, live events, sports, podcasts, and video games.

headline: Consumer Audio Market Size to Hit USD 412.08 Billion by 2035 | Research by SNS Insider
summary: The U.S. consumer audio market is expected to grow from $107.52 billion in 2025 to $412.08 billion by 2035, driven by wireless technology adoption, smart speakers, and premium audio demand. Headphones dominate with 38.65% market share, while soundbars show fastest growth at 16.85% CAGR. North America leads with 35.42% share, and Asia Pacific is the fastest-growing region at 16.55% CAGR. Market growth is tempered by saturation in mature segments and supply chain volatility.

headline: Is Alphabet Stock Going to $1,000?
summary: Alphabet stock could realistically reach $1,000 within a decade, up 225% from current levels of $307.65, driven by strong AI investments, dominant market positions in search and YouTube, and expected 12.7% annual EPS growth. The company's $175-185 billion capital expenditure in 2026 and 48% Google Cloud growth demonstrate its competitive strength.

headline: Socket Mobile Announces Industrial Scanning Solutions for iPhone 17e
summary: Socket Mobile announced that its industrial scanning solutions—XtremeScan, DuraSled, and DuraScan Terminal—are now compatible with Apple's newly released iPhone 17e. The company's rugged scanning devices integrate with the iPhone 17e's enhanced durability and performance for applications in warehousing, logistics, manufacturing, retail, and field service. Socket Mobile's CaptureSDK enables developers to quickly integrate support for the new device with minimal effort.

headline: Warren Buffett Recommends This 1 Investment to All Investors. Here's How It Could Help Build a Million-Dollar Portfolio.
summary: Warren Buffett recommends S&P 500 index funds, particularly the Vanguard S&P 500 ETF (VOO), as an ideal investment for non-professional investors seeking long-term wealth building. Through compound returns averaging 10% annually, an initial $900 investment plus $300 monthly contributions could exceed $1 million over 35 years. Buffett has emphasized this strategy in shareholder letters and even directed his trustee to invest 90% of his estate's cash in an S&P 500 index fund.

headline: Carahsoft’s Partner Pavilion Showcases Healthcare, AI and Cybersecurity Solutions at HIMSS26 in Las Vegas, NV on March 9-12, 2026
summary: Carahsoft Technology Corp. will showcase its healthcare IT solutions alongside more than 100 technology and reseller partners at the 2026 HIMSS Global Health Conference & Exhibition in Las Vegas (March 9-12). The event will feature keynote speakers including Jeremy Renner, Jon McNeill, Sumbul Ahmad Desai, and Mehmet Oz, with discussions on AI deployment in healthcare, cybersecurity, and interoperability. Carahsoft will host partner demonstrations, a networking reception, and a charity golf tournament supporting childhood cancer research.

headline: Which AI Stock is the Second Cheapest of the Magnificent Seven? The Answer May Surprise You.
summary: Nvidia has become the second cheapest stock among the Magnificent Seven at approximately 22x forward earnings, matching Meta's valuation. Despite being the key player in the AI revolution and delivering a blowout earnings report with 65% revenue growth to $215 billion, Nvidia's stock has pulled back along with other tech stocks due to investor concerns about AI revenue expectations and profit-taking. However, the pullback is not linked to weakening AI demand, and the article suggests this presents a buying opportunity for investors.

headline: Before Retiring, Warren Buffett Dumped $4.5 Billion Worth of 2 AI Stocks and Established a New Position in This 174-Year-Old Company
summary: Warren Buffett sold $4.5 billion in Apple and Amazon shares during his final quarter as CEO of Berkshire Hathaway, continuing a 13-quarter selling streak that accumulated $373 billion in cash. He simultaneously established a new position in The New York Times, a 174-year-old publisher that has successfully navigated digital transformation with strong subscriber growth and profitability.

headline: The Best "Magnificent Seven" Stocks to Buy in March
summary: The article analyzes the Magnificent Seven tech stocks, recommending Nvidia, Alphabet, Microsoft, Amazon, and Meta as strong March buys. Nvidia, Microsoft, and Meta trade at market-average valuations despite faster growth, while Amazon and Alphabet command premium valuations justified by their AI leadership and cloud computing dominance. Tesla and Apple are not recommended at current levels.

headline: 2 Warren Buffett Stocks to Buy Hand Over Fist This Month, and 1 to Avoid
summary: The article analyzes three Warren Buffett holdings: American Express is recommended as a buy despite a 20% pullback due to its strong position with affluent borrowers; Constellation Brands is suggested as a buying opportunity despite current weakness, as the beer industry is cyclical and the company is undergoing strategic improvements; DaVita is flagged as a stock to avoid due to deteriorating healthcare industry fundamentals and Berkshire's recent exit from the position.

headline: How Is It Possible That 78% of Vanguard's Equity ETFs Are Outperforming the S&P 500 in 2026?
summary: In 2026, the S&P 500 is down 0.2% year-to-date, underperforming 78% of Vanguard's equity ETFs. This reversal from 2023-2025 is driven by the concentration of the index in megacap growth stocks, particularly the Magnificent Seven, which are all down more than the broader index. Meanwhile, mid-caps, small-caps, value stocks, and international stocks are outperforming. The S&P 500 equal-weight index is up 5.3% YTD, showing that most individual S&P 500 components are actually gaining, but the largest companies are dragging down the market-cap-weighted index.

headline: 3 Unstoppable Tech Stocks to Buy Right Now for Less Than $1,000
summary: The article recommends three tech stocks from the Magnificent Seven that are trading under $1,000: Alphabet benefits from its dominant advertising business and fast-growing Google Cloud; Apple stands out for focusing on domestic manufacturing rather than massive AI infrastructure spending; and Nvidia is positioned as the primary beneficiary of AI chip spending across the industry.

headline: Consumer Tech News (March 2-6): Major Chip Earnings, Trump Refuted Negotiations With Anthropic AI & More
summary: The week saw major chip earnings reports with mixed results, geopolitical tensions around AI and Chinese tech investments, and significant corporate partnerships. Key developments include Broadcom and Marvell beating earnings expectations, the Trump administration refuting negotiations with Anthropic AI while imposing restrictions on its use, and major tech companies announcing AI infrastructure investments and content licensing deals.

headline: These 7 Elite Dividend Stocks Pay $114 Billion Annually, Combined, to Their Shareholders
summary: Seven major Wall Street companies collectively return over $114 billion annually to shareholders through dividends. Microsoft leads with $27.1 billion in annual payouts despite a low 0.9% yield, followed by ExxonMobil ($17.2B), JPMorgan Chase ($16.2B), Apple ($15.3B), Chevron ($14.1B), Johnson & Johnson ($12.5B), and Verizon ($11.94B). These dividend stocks have historically outperformed non-payers, with annualized returns of 9.2% versus 4.31% over 50+ years.

headline: Nvidia and Meta Platforms Are Now Cheaper Than the S&P 500. Which "Magnificent Seven" Stock Is the Best Buy in March?
summary: Nvidia and Meta Platforms are trading at valuations cheaper than the S&P 500 based on forward P/E ratios, presenting potential buying opportunities. Nvidia offers compelling value for investors believing in sustained earnings growth despite customer concentration risks, while Meta is capitalizing on AI monetization through its profitable app ecosystem. Both stocks are recommended as high-conviction buys for long-term investors.

headline: 3 Warning Signs Flashing in the Stock Market
summary: The stock market has rallied strongly toward record highs, but three warning signs suggest rising risks: narrow market leadership concentrated in mega-cap tech stocks, stretched valuations particularly in AI and technology sectors, and persistent interest rate uncertainty. While a major downturn isn't imminent, investors should monitor these vulnerabilities and maintain disciplined risk management.

headline: Warren Buffett Retired Having Not Purchased His Favorite Stock -- a Company He Spent $78 Billion Buying Over 6 Years -- in 19 Months
summary: Warren Buffett retired as Berkshire Hathaway CEO on December 31, 2025, after being a net seller of stocks for 13 consecutive quarters. Notably, he did not repurchase Berkshire Hathaway shares for 19 months before retirement, despite spending $78 billion on buybacks from July 2018 to June 2024. His successor Greg Abel has resumed share repurchases at more attractive valuations, demonstrating the same disciplined, value-focused investment philosophy.

headline: Apple Could Have Purchased Any of 488 S&P 500 Companies -- Instead, It's Made an Aggressive $841 Billion Investment
summary: Apple has invested $841 billion in share buybacks since fiscal 2013, reducing outstanding shares by 43.3% and boosting earnings per share. While this strategy has contributed to strong stock performance, the article argues it may be masking operational shortcomings, including slowing device sales growth and a valuation of 33x earnings compared to historical 10-15x multiples when growth was stronger.

headline: Cellhub Introduces Cellhub Managed Services at HIMSS to Power its “Hospitals Without Walls” Virtual Care Initiative
summary: Cellhub launched its AI-powered Cellhub Managed Services and 'Hospitals Without Walls' program at HIMSS 2026 to help rural hospitals deploy virtual clinical operations and expand care through 5G connectivity. The initiative addresses the rural healthcare crisis where 46% of rural hospitals operate at a loss by offering cost optimization, virtual care platforms, and new revenue opportunities through data partnerships.

headline: Smart Home Market Expected to Grow to $139.24 Billion by 2032
summary: The global smart home market is expected to grow from $95.83 billion in 2026 to $139.24 billion by 2032, driven by increasing demand for integrated home automation, IoT-enabled devices, and AI-enabled platforms. The entertainment and other controls segment leads the market, while retrofit installations are growing faster than new installations. Asia Pacific is projected to register the fastest growth at 9.0% CAGR.

headline: Why Palantir Is Soaring While Big Tech Tanks
summary: Palantir Technologies rallied 15% between February 27 and March 6 amid geopolitical tensions and a U.S. attack on Iran, bucking a broader market downturn. The company benefits from its 60% government revenue exposure and potential gains from the Pentagon's exclusion of Anthropic from contracts. Meanwhile, major tech and semiconductor stocks like Apple, Amazon, Alphabet, and Micron declined due to Middle East conflict concerns affecting supply chains and data center operations.

headline: 2 Warren Buffett Stocks To Buy Hand Over Fist and 1 To Avoid
summary: The article recommends Apple and American Express as strong long-term investments from Warren Buffett's portfolio, citing their durable business models and growth prospects. However, it advises avoiding Kraft Heinz, which faces declining revenues and has been one of Berkshire Hathaway's worst investments despite cost-cutting efforts and recent R&D investments.

headline: Is Berkshire Hathaway Being Too Patient With Its Cash?
summary: Berkshire Hathaway ended 2025 with $373.3 billion in cash and continued selling stocks for the 13th consecutive quarter, primarily divesting Apple and Bank of America holdings. The company did not repurchase shares for six straight quarters until recently, prompting investor frustration. New CEO Greg Abel emphasized patience and discipline in deploying capital, but concerns remain about Berkshire's lack of technology expertise as the sector dominates markets.

headline: Is Apple Stock a Buy Now?
summary: Apple unveiled the MacBook Neo at its March event, a $599 entry-level laptop that could significantly expand its addressable market in the PC space. With Mac products representing only 10% of Apple's $305 billion hardware sales, this new product could drive substantial growth. Despite a 70% surge in recent years, Apple trades at 30x earnings with expected 13% annual growth, making it a reasonable buy at current valuations.

headline: 3 Market Narratives That Could Break the Rally
summary: US equities have rallied toward record highs driven by AI enthusiasm, strong earnings, and economic resilience. However, three key narratives could derail the market: potential AI spending slowdowns leading to valuation pressure on tech stocks, persistently higher interest rates impacting growth-oriented sectors, and narrow market leadership concentrated in mega-cap tech companies. Investors should monitor these shifting narratives as they could trigger increased volatility.

headline: The PC Collapse Has a Winner -- and It's Not Who You Think
summary: Soaring memory chip prices driven by AI infrastructure demand are expected to severely hurt PC shipments in 2026, with prices surging 17% and shipments declining 10.4%. HP faces significant margin pressure with limited mitigation options, while Apple is strategically launching a budget MacBook Neo at $599 to capture Windows PC users during the memory crunch, positioning itself for stronger Mac market share growth.

headline: This Is How Much Berkshire Hathaway Made From Coca-Cola and American Express Dividends in 2025 Alone
summary: Berkshire Hathaway generated $816 million in dividends from Coca-Cola and $479 million from American Express in 2025 alone. These two longest-held positions, owned for nearly 40 years, demonstrate the power of dividend compounding with yield-on-cost of 65% for Coca-Cola and 44% for American Express, far exceeding current market yields.

headline: Nvidia, Apple 'Too Big, Too Soon'? Relax — This Same Thing Happened In The 1930s
summary: Market concentration concerns about the Magnificent Seven (Nvidia, Apple, Microsoft, Amazon, Alphabet, Meta, Tesla) controlling 30% of the S&P 500 are overblown, according to research from Elm Wealth. Historical data shows similar concentration levels existed in the 1930s, 1950s, and 1960s. Studies indicate concentration has no relationship with subsequent market risk or returns, and attempting to reduce exposure based on concentration fears destroys performance. However, valuations remain a separate concern, with expected long-term returns only 1% above inflation-protected bonds.

headline: Multi Window Processor Market Size to Surpass USD 4.81 Billion by 2035 | Research by SNS Insider
summary: The U.S. multi-window processor market is expected to grow at a CAGR of 10.31% through 2035, driven by AI integration, rising demand in automotive (digital cockpits, ADAS), healthcare, and broadcasting sectors. Hardware currently dominates with 68.50% market share, while software is the fastest-growing segment. North America leads with 36.70% global share, with Asia Pacific showing the highest growth potential.

headline: 2 Stocks That Will Be Worth More Than Apple by 2028
summary: The article argues that Microsoft and Alphabet will surpass Apple in market value by 2028 due to stronger growth rates, superior AI capabilities, and higher net income. While Apple recently rallied to become the world's second-largest company, the author contends it lacks innovation and lags in the AI arms race. Both Microsoft and Alphabet benefit from rapidly growing cloud computing segments (Azure up 39% YoY, Google Cloud up 48% YoY) and trade at lower valuations despite generating more net income than Apple.

headline: SVP Sells Qorvo 8,226 Shares Worth $683,000
summary: Frank P. Stewart, SVP of Advanced Cellular at Qorvo, sold 8,226 shares worth approximately $683,000 on February 17, 2026, reducing his direct holdings by 19.18%. Despite the sale, Stewart retained over 80% of his shares, suggesting confidence in the company. The transaction comes as Qorvo shows gradual improvement after bottoming in spring 2025, with a 10.67% gain over the past year.

headline: Mophie Introduces Premium Soft Goods Collection for iPhone, iPad, MacBook, and AirTag
summary: Mophie, a ZAGG brand, launched a new collection of premium accessories for Apple devices including iPhone cases, iPad folio covers, AirTag accessories, and MacBook hardshell cases. The lineup features design-forward products with premium materials, MagSafe compatibility, and a two-year warranty, available at Apple retail stores, Apple.com, and Mophie.com.

headline: Apple Free Cash Flow Surge Supports $293 Price Target Debate
summary: Apple delivered exceptional Q1 2026 results with $143.76B revenue (up 15.65% YoY), free cash flow surging 169.57% to $43.64B, and gross margins expanding to 48.2%. The company is benefiting from strong iPhone 17 demand, a 38% revenue surge in China, and emerging AI agent hardware demand for Mac products without significant capex. Analyst price targets range from $267 to $324, with the primary target at $293. Key risks include iPhone supply constraints from TSMC and delayed AI Siri rollout.

headline: Greg Abel Has Over 60% of Berkshire Hathaway's Stock Portfolio Invested in 9 Forever Stocks
summary: Greg Abel, Warren Buffett's successor at Berkshire Hathaway, identified nine core holdings that represent over 60% of the company's stock portfolio and plans to hold them indefinitely. These include Apple, American Express, Coca-Cola, Moody's, and five Japanese trading houses (Mitsubishi, Mitsui, Itochu, Sumitomo, and Marubeni). Abel expects limited trading activity in these positions going forward.

headline: 2 No-Brainer Warren Buffett Stocks to Buy Right Now
summary: The article recommends Apple and Alphabet as two attractive Warren Buffett stocks to buy. Apple benefits from its strong brand loyalty, deep ecosystem, and growing services segment, with recent double-digit revenue growth. Alphabet offers opportunities in its core advertising business, cloud computing, and AI, with Google Cloud growing at 48% year-over-year and a $240 billion backlog.

headline: Does Apple Have a New Hit on Its Hands?
summary: Apple announced new MacBook Pro, monitors, and the MacBook Neo, a $599 budget laptop using the A18 Pro chip designed to compete with Chromebooks and Windows PCs. While the Neo targets new markets and families, analysts debate whether it represents meaningful innovation or just mature company refinement. The discussion also covers AI's future role in hardware and airline stocks facing headwinds from rising oil prices.

headline: Growing Your Income vs. Maximizing It Now: The Core Difference Between VIG and HDV
summary: VIG and HDV are two dividend-focused ETFs with different strategies: VIG tracks companies with proven dividend growth histories across 338 holdings with a tech and financial tilt, yielding 1.6%, while HDV concentrates on 74 high-yielding stocks in defensive sectors like energy and consumer staples, yielding 2.9%. VIG offers lower costs (0.04% expense ratio) and better long-term total returns, while HDV provides higher current income but with less diversification and lower five-year performance.

headline: FDVV vs. HDV: 2 High-Dividend ETFs With Opposite Ideas About Big Tech
summary: FDVV and HDV are high-dividend ETFs with nearly identical yields but strikingly different approaches. FDVV includes tech giants like Nvidia, Apple, and Microsoft alongside traditional dividend stocks, charging a higher expense ratio but delivering stronger 5-year returns (60.3% vs 42.3%). HDV takes a defensive stance, focusing on energy, healthcare, and consumer staples with lower fees and less volatility. The choice depends on investor preference: FDVV suits those seeking growth with income, while HDV appeals to income-first investors preferring traditional sectors.
